items.title: Ira Gitler interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995
items.q: I heard Jimmy Heath’s big band recently

ctx.x: Can — and this is kind of a follow-up — can jazz, you know for instance we talk about the big band period and we say how two great things, people were dancing and people were listening on the radio. Can jazz ever become America’s popular music again?

Looking at it right now, I don’t think so, but who knows? That was a particular time, if you’re talking about big bands, you know economically it’s not feasible. In fact if you have a sextet and you want to book it, you’re probably better off cutting it back to a quintet because you might have a better chance, right? And big bands exist now in little places once a week or some bands have existed getting bookings, you know going to Europe and Japan and all that, but the big band is not a viable thing. Once…

Yeah, I wanted to ask you perhaps maybe just one last question here and that is you know students hopefully, the students even at our college and perhaps even other colleges, will see these tapes. Tell us a few things that students should know about jazz, other than just the names and dates.
